items.headline: U.S. FBI intelligence agent arrested in connection with theft of $1 million in crypto
items.subheadline: The agent, who had "top secret" clearance and worked in FBI headquarters, was accused of taking crypto from wallets the agency had investigated.
items.author: Jesse Hamilton

items.headline: The systemic-risk debate over perpetual futures is aimed at the wrong target
items.subheadline: As perpetuals enter regulated markets, critics warn they import systemic risk. But the risk comes from venue design — leverage limits, margin rules, index construction, and default handling — not the contract itself, argues Chris Tyrer, President of Bullish Exchange.
items.author: Chris Tyrer

items.headline: Everything is becoming a perp
items.subheadline: The perpetual — the 24/7, leveraged contract that crypto invented and then perfected — is no longer just a way to trade crypto, says Katana Network’s Matthew Fisher. It’s becoming the way to trade everything.
items.author: Matthew Fisher

items.headline: RWA perps will outpace tokenization
items.subheadline: Tokenization was crypto's first big export to TradFi. Perps are next, says Martin Lee, markets insight lead at DWF labs.
items.author: Martin Lee

items.headline: Everyone has the perps convergence backwards
items.subheadline: Crypto is said to be growing up to look like Wall Street. The evidence in its biggest market points the other way, argues Bitget CEO Gracy Chen.
items.author: Gracy Chen

items.headline: BlackRock (BLK) debuts tokenized access to $311 billion of money market funds in Europe
items.subheadline: Earlier this week, BlackRock expanded its U.S. tokenized cash platform which involved offering onchain shares of an existing fund, plus a new daily reinvestment stablecoin fund.
items.author: Ian Allison

items.headline: BTC price rises as Coldcard exploit, Strategy sales recede. ADA advances: Crypto Markets Today
items.subheadline: Bitcoin advanced as the market settled down following the weekend’s hack of Coldcard wallets and sales by Strategy even as sentiment remained in “extreme fear.”
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: South African lawmakers propose draft rules on cross-border crypto transactions
items.subheadline: A draft rulebook proposes that sending crypto offshore must be conducted through an authorized provider and be reported to the central bank’s FinSurv.
items.author: Jamie Crawley

items.headline: The bitcoin (BTC) price has plenty of reasons to freak out, yet volatility remains low: Crypto Daily
items.subheadline: The day ahead in crypto: Aug. 4, 2026
items.author: Omkar Godbole

items.headline: New York sues Kalshi, will seek damages, alleging it offers gambling platform
items.subheadline: The state is seeking a penalty equal to three times Kalshi’s gains from the activity, plus $100,000 for each unauthorized or attempted offer of sports or mobile sports wagering,.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: The UK has finally shown it’s serious about crypto
items.subheadline: Several recent regulatory steps indicate the UK might finally stop dragging its feet when it comes to crypto, argues Wirex CEO Chet Shah.
items.author: Chet Shah

items.headline: Ethereum enters its second decade after a year of upheaval at the foundation
items.subheadline: Few periods in Ethereum's 11-year history have brought as much change, from leadership shakeups at the Ethereum Foundation to institutional adoption, as the past year has.
items.author: Margaux Nijkerk

items.headline: Circle (CRCL) slides after Morgan Stanley slashes price target to $38 from $106
items.subheadline: The bank said tokenized money market funds, Open USD and slower USDC growth could weigh on the stablecoin issuer's earnings.
items.author: Helene Braun

items.headline: Trump-backed American Bitcoin (ABTC) executive Matt Prusak joins Giga Energy
items.subheadline: The executive is leaving the Eric Trump-backed miner to join an AI power infrastructure firm, highlighting the shift toward energy and data center buildout.
items.author: Will Canny

items.headline: Live updates: Bitcoin stuck in tight range as risk assets soar on Iran deal hopes
items.subheadline: Japan may have spent as much as $36.6 billion buying yen in the first joint US-Japan action to support the currency since 1998. Bitget Wallet’s Alvin Kan says it can slow a disorderly slide without reversing the broader trend.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Hashdex to close U.S. spot BTC ETF as inflows concentrate, investors chase AI returns
items.subheadline: DEFI held $14.7 million, versus $142.4 million for BTCW and $47.08 billion for BlackRock’s IBIT.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: U.S.-Japan yen intervention revives bitcoin carry trade fears despite weak link
items.subheadline: Coordinated action sent the yen sharply higher, but bitcoin’s recent correlation suggests U.S. dollar strength, rather than the carry trade, may be the bigger risk.
items.author: James Van Straten

items.headline: BTC news: A bitcoin wallet dormant since 2013 moved $31 million
items.subheadline: A dormant bitcoin wallet holding $31 million moved for the first time since 2013, amid a wave of old coins shifting on-chain following the Coldcard hardware wallet hack.
items.author: Omkar Godbole

items.headline: BTC, ETH, SOL price news: Bitcoin nears $64,000 as traders look past Strategy's BTC sales
items.subheadline: Every major token except ether is green on the week, with BTC up 1.9% over 24 hours and Asian equities selling off on AI-trade jitters.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: XRP holders can now borrow RLUSD on Ethereum through $280 million lending pool
items.subheadline: XRP holders can now borrow RLUSD against their coins on Ethereum without selling, through a $280 million vault that had never accepted an XRP-linked asset before.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Why Jim Cramer’s quantum panic isn’t rattling bitcoin (BTC) as price holds around $64,000
items.subheadline: Jim Cramer says he's dumping his bitcoin over quantum computing fears, but his track record of crypto and bank calls has buoyed the crypto community.
items.author: Omkar Godbole

items.headline: Bhutan's Gelephu Mindfulness City puts part of its BTC treasury to work after 10,000 bitcoin pledge
items.subheadline: The planned Gelephu Mindfulness City says 3iQ will run part of its bitcoin treasury on a market-neutral basis, a shift from holding the coins as a long-term national asset.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Why Aave proposes quitting 6 blockchains that earn under $5,000 a quarter
items.subheadline: A governance proposal would shut deployments on Sonic, Scroll, zkSync, Metis, Soneium and Aptos, and retire 50 asset markets elsewhere. Deposits on some have fallen more than 90%.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Major bitcoin wallet flaw drains 594 BTC in 25-minute sweep
items.subheadline: A hardware wallet randomness bug turned “impossible to guess” seeds into guessable ones, and $38 million is already gone.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: How bitcoin cold wallets lost $70 million in an attack that never touched the devices
items.subheadline: Galaxy Research said weak seed generation let an attacker recreate likely private keys offline, sweep more than 1,000 BTC from nearly 1,200 wallets and continue searching without ever accessing the devices.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Ripple news: XRP Ledger upgrade brings back features once pulled over critical bugs
items.subheadline: The xrpld 3.3.0 release is expected next week with five proposed amendments, including two revised features that were previously withdrawn after researchers found bugs that could have allowed unauthorized transactions or fee draining.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Solana (SOL) news: Foundation's new CISO warns AI is making crypto scams more convincing
items.subheadline: Michael Coates, the foundation’s new CISO, said that AI vulnerabilities and fake identities will drive the next wave of blockchain security concerns.
items.author: Margaux Nijkerk

items.headline: Bitcoin cold-wallet attack spreads to 4,500 addresses as losses near $89 million
items.subheadline: Galaxy Research flagged a third wave of sweeps tied to weak Coldcard-generated keys, with the attacker now targeting smaller balances and changing how funds are collected onchain.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Legacy crypto on-ramps and bridges will disappear as payments become invisible, Fun CEO says
items.subheadline: Alex Fine said standalone crypto payment rails are becoming obsolete as platforms shift toward unified funding flows that abstract away blockchain complexity for users.
items.author: Will Canny

items.headline: Bitcoin cold-wallet losses may near $114 million as possible fourth sweep emerges
items.subheadline: The pending transactions signal replace-by-fee, so anyone who spots their address in the mempool has minutes to pay a higher fee and move funds first.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: A new Solana proposal would take daily SOL burns from $47,000 to $650,000
items.subheadline: SGP-0003 bundles a fee overhaul with a doubling of the disinflation rate. It needs 40 million more SOL of validator support in two weeks to reach a vote.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: The Clarity Act isn't a ticket to sanctions evasion, actually
items.subheadline: The bill, as currently drafted, has the power to stop sanctions evasion at scale, argues Ari Redbord, global head of policy at TRM Labs.
items.author: Ari Redbord

items.headline: The privacy paradox of protecting kids online
items.subheadline: We don’t need to imagine the privacy pitfalls of age verification. They’ve been happening for years, argues Cardano Foundation CEO Frederik Gregaard.
items.author: Frederik Gregaard

items.headline: The Clarity Act is the most important consumer protection effort in years
items.subheadline: Consumers should not have to wait for another crisis to get the protections they deserve, argues Summer Mersinger, CEO of the Blockchain Association.
items.author: Summer Mersinger

items.headline: AI is destroying the internet. Math is our only hope.
items.subheadline: The rise of autonomous AI agents necessitates the utilization of zero-knowledge proofs, argues Brian Trunzo, chief growth officer at Succinct Labs.
items.author: Brian Trunzo

items.headline: The KIDS Act is way worse than digital carding — it is a mass surveillance system
items.subheadline: The fact that lawmakers are even contemplating a bill that would create a surveillance and censorship regime should be a wake-up call for everyone who values privacy and free expression, argues Electronic Frontier Foundation's India McKinney.
items.author: India McKinney

items.headline: Democratizing weather derivatives through tokenization could be blockchain industry’s most important real-world use case
items.subheadline: Main Street, which faces the most significant climate-related financial risk, currently lacks an avenue to hedge weather-related risks, argues CoinDesk’s Omkar Godbole.
items.author: Omkar Godbole

items.headline: SpaceX is a battleground Solana must win
items.subheadline: Perps are a trojan horse to bring all of traditional finance onchain, argues Brian Smith, president of the Jito Foundation.
items.author: Brian Smith

items.headline: U.S. sanctions Iran-linked bitcoin insurance scheme for Strait of Hormuz ships
items.subheadline: The Treasury Department said the Hormuz Safe platform accepted bitcoin and other digital assets as part of an alleged sanctions workaround tied to IRGC-backed shipping controls.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Circle secures New York trust charter as crypto regulatory push accelerates
items.subheadline: The approval lets the USDC issuer offer fiduciary and custody services under New York banking law.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: SEC to review Nasdaq bitcoin options approval after CME challenge
items.subheadline: CME argues that because bitcoin is a commodity, options tied to its value fall under CFTC jurisdiction, not the SEC's authority.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: Counting down the days: State of Crypto
items.subheadline: The Senate is going on its summer break in a week, leaving next to no time left to sort out its remaining priorities in August. And obviously, the fate of Clarity is one of those priorities.
items.author: Nikhilesh De

items.headline: Robinhood wins UK crypto registration ahead of new regulatory regime commencing
items.subheadline: Robinhood’s U.K. arm has been added to the FCA's list of registered cryptoasset companies as of July 31.
items.author: Jamie Crawley

items.headline: Bitget notifies users of end to crypto trading services in Japan
items.subheadline: The Seychelles-based crypto exchange did not share specific reasons for shutting down operations in Japan.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: Bernstein warns Clarity Act failure could spark another crypto selloff
items.subheadline: The broker said failure to pass the Clarity Act this year would likely send crypto lower, but expects U.S. regulators to accelerate rulemaking.
items.author: Will Canny

items.headline: BTC news: Coldcard urges users to move bitcoin as active wallet exploit continues
items.subheadline: The cold wallet maker said the flaw behind roughly $114 million in losses remains live, with specific models and firmware still exposed.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: BNY to add crypto staking to digital asset custody platform
items.subheadline: The custody bank has selected Galaxy to provide staking infrastructure as it broadens services for institutional crypto investors.
items.author: Helene Braun

items.headline: BitGo’s WBTC move pushes LayerZero-to-Chainlink tally near $15 billion
items.subheadline: A migration wave followed a $292 million Kelp bridge exploit, with announced LayerZero-to-Chainlink moves now totaling $14.5 billion.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: As Clarity Act teeters, mystery group hammers away at crypto in Washington ads
items.subheadline: Crypto Watchdog has taken to warning people in DC about the hazards of digital assets, and its director won't say who is backing it.
items.author: Jesse Hamilton

items.headline: Dinari brings tokenized U.S. stocks to American investors as equity race heats up
items.subheadline: The move brings the custodial tokenization model to eligible U.S. investors as competition over blockchain-based equities intensifies.
items.author: Krisztian Sandor

items.headline: Banking giant Intesa Sanpaolo cuts IBIT stake 94%, triples ether ETF holding
items.subheadline: Its iShares Staked Ethereum Trust ETF (ETHB) stake tripled to 349,600 shares as long bitcoin ETF holdings fell 35% in value to $69.3 million.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: Polymarket targets $20 billion valuation as competition heats up in prediction market sector
items.subheadline: The blockchain-based prediction markets platform is reportedly returning to investors months after a $15 billion funding round.
items.author: Helene Braun

items.headline: Bitcoin (BTC) price analysis: $63,000 level is key
items.subheadline: Retail investors and large whales are buying as bitcoin trades near its 200-week moving average.
items.author: James Van Straten

items.headline: Wells Fargo joins JPMorgan and Citi in the race to tokenize Wall Street’s settlement rails
items.subheadline: Payments will run on the bank’s proprietary blockchain and be routed automatically through its existing client interface.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: Clarity Act sits idle over Trump ethics question as Warren asks SEC to investigate him
items.subheadline: Senators Elizabeth Warren and Richard Blumenthal requested the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission probe Trump's memecoin.
items.author: Jesse Hamilton

items.headline: Samsung is bringing stablecoins to 800 million phones in a massive crypto bet
items.subheadline: By baking digital dollar tools straight into its native wallet app, the tech giant is solving one of Web3's biggest distribution hurdles.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: Why Visa, Mastercard and Coinbase aren't abandoning USDC stablecoin for Open USD
items.subheadline: Executives at Coinbase, Visa and Mastercard said they plan to support multiple stablecoins, suggesting Open USD is another payments rail rather than a direct replacement for USDC.
items.author: Krisztian Sandor

items.headline: Elon Musk's SpaceX (SPCX) tops earnings as bitcoin (BTC) holding value drops by $540 million
items.subheadline: Elon Musk's space company posted its first earnings as a public company ahead of a major insider share unlock.
items.author: Krisztian Sandor

items.headline: Bitcoin is 49% below its record while the S&P 500 hits all-time highs
items.subheadline: BTC held near $64,000 as MSCI's world index set another peak and Brent fell toward a Hormuz deal. Ether is the only major down on the week.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Coldcard hacker's $36 million bitcoin (BTC) wallet becomes a graffiti wall of pleas and hustles
items.subheadline: The Coldcard hacker's bitcoin wallet has turned into a graffiti wall of pleas, poetry and scams, as victims and opportunists pay to leave permanent messages using Bitcoin's OP_RETURN function.
items.author: Omkar Godbole

items.headline: New Ethereum proposal would cut issuance to zero if staked ETH reaches $112 billion
items.subheadline: The EIP-8361 draft proposal calls for burning a rising share of validator rewards as the staking ratio climbs.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa
